chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad bin Ali al-Kufi, from Ubaidullah al-Dahqan, from Darust bin Abi Mansur al-Wasiti, from Ibrahim bin Abdil-Hamid, from Abu'l-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have taught my son this book (writing/literacy), so for what thing shall I give it (as payment/give him as a gift)? He said: Give it, for the sake of Allah, to your father, and do not give it to five: do not give it to an evil-wisher, nor a goldsmith, nor a slaughterer, nor a wheat seller, nor a slave trader.

Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is an evil-wisher? He said: The one who sells winding sheets and wishes for the death of my nation, whereas the one born from my nation is more beloved to me than what the sun has shined upon.
As for the goldsmith, he treats the fraud of my nation.
As for the slaughterer, he slaughters until mercy departs his heart.
As for the wheat seller, he corners food from my nation, whereas for a servant to meet Allah as a thief is more beloved to me than if he meets Him having cornered food for forty days.
As for the slave trader, indeed, Jibra'eel (peace be upon him) came to me and said: O Muhammad, indeed, the evil ones from your nation are those who sell people.

key_terms.السِّيَاءُ: Evil-wisher; one who sells winding sheets and wishes for the death of others

ai.seo_question: What are the five types of people the Prophet advised against giving one's son to, and why?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) identifies five specific professions—evil-wishers, goldsmiths, butchers, grain hoarders, and slave traders—as detrimental to a child's spiritual and moral development due to their inherent ethical failings. This guidance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on selecting mentors who cultivate mercy and justice, contrasting the spiritual decay of these trades with the Prophet’s love for his Ummah. The warning against slave trading is notably linked to the appearance of Jibril, underscoring the divine validation of these social critiques.

My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ahmad bin Abi Abdillah, from Muhammed ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Ubaidullah al-Dahqan, from Darast bin Abi Mansur al-Wasiti, from Ibrahim ibn Abdil-Hamid, from Abu’l-Hasan, Musa, peace be upon him, that he said:

A man came to the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, and said: O Messenger of Allah, I have taught my son this book, so for what thing shall I give it? He said: Give it, for the sake of Allah, to your father, and do not give it to five: do not give it to an evil-wisher, nor a goldsmith, nor a slaughterer, nor a wheat seller, nor a slave trader.

Then he said: O Messenger of Allah, and what is an evil-wisher? He said: The one who sells winding sheets and wishes for the death of my nation, whereas the one born from my nation is more beloved to me than what the sun has shined upon.
As for the goldsmith, he treats the fraud of my nation.
As for the slaughterer, he slaughters until mercy departs his heart.
As for the wheat seller, he corners food from my nation, whereas for a servant to meet Allah as a thief is more beloved to me than if he meets Him having cornered food for forty days.
As for the slave trader, indeed, Jibra’eel, peace be upon him, came to me and said: O Muhammed, indeed, the evil ones from your nation are those who sell people.
